name: 京都ラーメン きんざん 七条本店 (Kyoto Ramen Kinzan Shichijo Honten)

claims.text: Wheat ramen noodles are boiled in shared water, and the soy-sauce tare is wheat-based, so gluten contact is inherent to every bowl.
The black soup is seasoned with aged soy sauce (from Oyama and Goko breweries), which is wheat-based.
Broth is pork-bone based and finished with back fat; pork chashu tops the bowls, so there is no vegan-safe preparation line.

name: 京都鶏白湯そば 純 四条烏丸 (Kyoto Toripaitan Soba Jun Shijo-Karasuma)

claims.text: The shoyu and miso seasoning variants of the chicken-paitan soba are based on tare/sauces that conventionally contain wheat; no wheat-free seasoning is indicated.
All broths are animal-based (chicken paitan plus pork bones) and bowls are topped with pork chashu, so there is no vegan-safe preparation; cross-contact with meat and animal stock is inherent.

name: 京都和麺 諭吉本舗 (Kyoto Wamen Yukichi Honpo)

claims.text: Bowls use a soy-sauce / dashi tare typical of Japanese chuka-soba, which standardly contains wheat-based soy sauce; no wheat-free tare is advertised.

name: 魔界系ラーメン三冠馬 (Makaikei Ramen Sankanba)

claims.text: The bowls use a soy-based (shoyu) tare, which in Japanese ramen is virtually always wheat-containing soy sauce.
The bowl is described as a 醤油 (soy sauce) shoyu tare over Kyoto pork clear broth; standard Japanese shoyu is wheat-based, so the tare should be assumed to contain wheat.
Broth is pork-bone clear soup and toppings include pork chashu; evening dishes center on chicken and pork, indicating heavy animal-product use throughout the kitchen.

name: まる担 おがわ (Marutan Ogawa)

claims.text: Tantanmen here is made with wheat noodles in a sesame/miso/pork-based broth; this style of tare is wheat-based, so the dish is not gluten-free and no GF handling is indicated.
Broth and toppings are meat-based (ground meat plus a pork/sesame/miso broth), so vegan diners cannot be accommodated.

name: 麺スター む・ラッキー (Men Star Mu-Lucky)

claims.text: The tori-shoyu bowl is built on a sweet soy-sauce tare, which in Japanese ramen is virtually always wheat-based soy sauce.

name: 麺や 鳥の鶏次 KYOTO 四条河原町店 (Men-ya Tori no Keiji KYOTO Shijo Kawaramachi)

claims.text: Tori-shoyu (soy-sauce) bowls use a soy-based tare; Japanese shoyu is normally brewed with wheat. No gluten-free tare is advertised.
All broths are chicken-based (chicken + water simmered 8+ hours) and toppings include chicken chashu, so there is no vegan-safe preparation; cross-contact with animal stock is inherent to every bowl.
